steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: follow readiness into a durable command
steps.detail: Delivery scheduling is not simply an action attached to successful payment. Follow the reviewed chef-acceptance/ready-for-pickup event into DeliveryCommandScheduler, the durable command record and DeliveryCommandWorker. The scheduler tests describe a reviewed scheduling offset before readyAt and acceleration of an unattempted command when food becomes ready. Treat that as pinned implementation behavior, not authority to change commercial timing rules. A command is the durable instruction to attempt work; a provider job is evidence that an external booking exists; rider assignment and completed delivery are later facts. Draw these states separately. Changing a dashboard label cannot create a rider, and a queued command is not proof that a provider accepted a job.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: protect uncertain external outcomes
steps.detail: DeliveryCommandWorkerTest shows three materially different cases. An already existing job completes a redelivered command without invoking the router. An uncertain create outcome is stored for reconciliation instead of immediately creating another booking. A temporarily unavailable provider can defer work rather than treating every outage as a permanent dead letter. Understand the claim/lease and completion boundaries before changing retry logic. An exception after an external request may leave a real booking behind, even if no response arrived. Do not use a new client reference or fallback provider blindly when the original create outcome is uncertain.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: prove that retries do not book twice
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/integration-service/pom.xml -Dtest=DeliveryCommandSchedulerTest,DeliveryCommandWorkerTest test. Read completesRedeliveredCommandWithoutCallingProviderWhenJobAlreadyExists and the verifyNoInteractions assertion. Trace storesUncertainCreateForReconciliationWithoutRetryingTheProvider into the worker. In a local training branch add a mock assertion that a duplicate command cannot make a provider-create call. Draw timelines for scheduled, ready-now, duplicate and uncertain requests, using synthetic order and command IDs. The exercise must not publish a live broker message, book a rider or call a production provider endpoint.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: four dispatch timelines, the relevant mock assertions and a clear distinction between command queued, provider job created, rider assigned and delivered.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: readiness is a gate before ranking
steps.detail: Read DeliveryIntelligenceService with the router and provider-readiness code. Identify how candidates become eligible, which observations are available before booking and which ranking components are actually used. A configured adapter name must not bypass production approval, correct environment, contract completeness or enabled execution controls. A ranking score is a decision aid among eligible candidates, not an authorization to invoke a disabled vendor. Inspect the persistence of candidate/decision context so an operator can explain why a provider was selected. Do not invent proximity or rider ETA when the provider cannot supply it before booking; the repository includes a neutral-proximity regression for that situation.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: model signals are not ground truth
steps.detail: Distinguish a fixed heuristic, probabilistic sampling and feedback updated from observed outcomes. Do not describe a heuristic as a trained production model without training/evaluation evidence. A provider having a high score does not prove its current API is healthy or its service is hyperlocal. Keep actual selection, fallback selection and final booked provider coherent in the persisted decision. Missing outcomes, duplicate callbacks and changing provider coverage can bias feedback. Before changing weights or business ranking policy, obtain the approved rule; Academy may explain the code and test boundedness but must not make that product decision.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: explain one synthetic selection
steps.detail: Create a table of three fictional candidate responses: eligible with quote, configured but execution disabled, and temporarily unavailable. Trace which candidates are filtered before scoring. For the remaining candidate, list each score input and identify whether it is observed, neutral or derived. Read DeliveryIntelligenceNeutralProximityTest and the predictor/scorer tests in the Integration test tree. Build a counterexample showing why a superior score must not override a readiness failure. Deliver a synthetic decision record with selected provider, eligibility evidence, score explanation and missing-data notes. Do not change live ranking weights, enable a provider or manufacture a successful delivery outcome.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: an eligibility-before-ranking explanation and a scored example with honest missing inputs. Model or ranking output must never be presented as proof of production activation.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: close the delivery feedback loop
steps.detail: Trace a delivery through command creation, provider adapter, persisted job/reference, webhook or status polling, normalized status update, Order projection and feedback processing. Each boundary has its own identity and evidence. Provider status codes must be mapped using that provider's contract rather than copied from another courier. Read DeliveryFeedbackWorkerTest and its implementation to identify deduplication, eligibility and persistence behavior before explaining how an outcome influences future decisions. A displayed delivery history and a model-feedback record are different views of the same lifecycle. A dashboard should reveal missing or delayed data, not invent a complete journey when one source is unavailable.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: history, filters and delayed status
steps.detail: For missing dashboard data, separate source availability from request filters and presentation. The repository contains regressions for all-time, thirty-day and custom history windows, and for SQL sort construction. A successful request covering a recent window does not prove older history was deleted. Capture the exact hours/date range, pagination offsets, sort and limit before investigating. For delayed tracking, check provider reference, callback acceptance, normalized event, consumer state and projection timestamp in order. Do not recreate a delivery to make its tracking timeline look fresh, and do not let a stale event overwrite a terminal delivery state.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: reconstruct one synthetic delivery across systems
steps.detail: Create a ledger containing chef sub-order ID, command ID, provider job reference, provider callback identity, normalized status event and feedback outcome. Mark the first missing checkpoint in three variants: no provider booking, booking exists but callback delayed, and normalized status exists but the dashboard filter excludes it. Run the focused worker/scheduler tests and read the feedback tests. For history investigation use mocked controller/repository tests, not production exports. State which tests prove duplicate safety and which only prove filtering. Deliver a diagnosis that names the failing boundary rather than saying delivery is broken.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a complete booking-to-feedback map and three narrow diagnoses. Neither CI success nor a nonempty dashboard proves real rider assignment for every order.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: implement an adapter without inventing a vendor API
steps.detail: A hyperlocal provider integration needs an approved real contract for authentication, serviceability/quote, create, cancel, status, callbacks, references and error semantics. Read the existing provider adapter interface, router and PidgeApiClientTest to learn the Craves integration boundary. Keep vendor-specific payloads and status mapping inside the adapter; the rest of Craves consumes its normalized contract. Document staging and production separately and verify that the contracted service is truly instant/intracity/hyperlocal, not a similarly branded parcel product. No missing endpoint, key format or webhook signature rule may be invented. An existing portal account or commercial activation does not prove Craves has a usable API contract.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: define the uncertain-create branch
steps.detail: Specify timeout budgets, stable client references, response validation, duplicate prevention and reconciliation before enabling create. Authentication failure, no serviceability, rate limiting, temporary outage, invalid payload and unknown external outcome require different normalized results. A fallback is safe only when the first provider is known not to have created a job or the established reconciliation logic permits it. Preserve the actual fallback provider in job/decision records. Require verified callback origin/authenticity and duplicate handling appropriate to the approved vendor contract. Keep credentials in the established secret store and never include them in adapter code, fixtures or course content.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: build a local fake hyperlocal adapter
steps.detail: Training-only task: implement a fake adapter behind the existing interface in a local branch, with no network client and no registration in production configuration. It returns deterministic synthetic quote/create/status outcomes so you can test router behavior. Provide fixtures for success, unavailable, invalid response, rate limit, duplicate command and uncertain create. Use the existing command worker tests as the model for asserting provider calls do not repeat. Run PidgeApiClientTest only as the repository's isolated test suite after inspecting its fixture setup; do not point it at a real endpoint. Submit interface mapping, full fake implementation, tests, readiness checklist and a release plan that leaves production execution disabled.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a working local fake adapter and failure matrix, plus an explicit list of real vendor facts still required for any new production provider. The exercise neither activates nor changes Pidge, Borzo, Shadowfax or Delhivery.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: use progressively stronger evidence
steps.detail: Adapter unit tests, command persistence tests, isolated callback tests, approved staging acceptance and a controlled real hyperlocal job establish different properties. Keep source-ready, configured, enabled, routable and production-accepted as distinct states in release records. Before a provider release, inspect the current approved provider path and record its immutable image, configuration and rollback evidence. A curriculum update must not redeploy Integration or reconfigure providers. The current one-replica posture remains unchanged; concurrency/recovery tests can reveal risks, but they do not justify a silent infrastructure scale-out or a promise of unlimited future load.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: reconcile the job already created
steps.detail: When create times out, inspect command state and the existing provider reference through the approved read/reconciliation path. Do not immediately choose another vendor. When polling or callbacks lag, preserve the booking and repair the normalized-status pipeline rather than deleting evidence. Stop on duplicate bookings, conflicting provider references, unauthorized callbacks or unexplained terminal-state reversals. Recovery must retain command attempts, job identity, callback history and the reason for manual intervention. A provider-disable or code rollback decision is narrow containment; cancellation of a real rider job has external consequences and requires the relevant operational authorization.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: run a failure rehearsal with no real deliveries
steps.detail: Run mvn -B -ntp -f services/integration-service/pom.xml -Dtest=DeliveryCommandWorkerTest,DeliveryCommandSchedulerTest,PidgeApiClientTest,DeliveryFeedbackWorkerTest test after confirming the selected tests use local mocks/fixtures. Prepare tabletop cases for redelivery, unknown create outcome, all providers unavailable, delayed callback and dashboard filter mismatch. For each, include expected state, provider-call count, safe next read, abort condition and narrow recovery. Record any skipped database cases honestly. No real webhook replay, production load test, paid provider call or live assignment is part of the lab. Finish with a peer review of the evidence rather than relying on the two reading questions.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a reproducible mock test run, failure-state matrix and recovery plan that cannot book twice. Live hyperlocal acceptance remains separate evidence and is never inferred from the course or a green build.
